At present, legally we are under no obligation to report stolen cars to the police.
General clause in UA Criminal Code ([Стаття 396. Приховування злочину|https://protocol.ua/ua/kriminalniy_kodeks_ukraini_stattya_396/]) prohibits *_active_* actions performed *_knowingly_* to hide the crime, such as helping the criminal to hide himself, object of the crime, evidence, tools used. Further, l*_iability arises only if someone helps to hide crimes punishable for more than 5 years in prison_*, whilst ordinary (without aggravating circumstances) illegal possession of a vehicle is punishable with 3-5 years ([Стаття 289. Незаконне заволодіння транспортним засобом|https://protocol.ua/ua/kriminalniy_kodeks_ukraini_stattya_289/]). This means that even in a situation where A. illegally possesses a car and B. helps him to hide this car in B’s garage, B is not criminally liable.
There’s currently no special law regulating ride-hailing business in Ukraine, and *_we are under no obligation to check if the car is reported as stolen_*. We can do it if we want though.
Thus, from a purely legal perspective Bolt and its officials are not breaching any laws if we do not report it to the police.Still, from the business and PR perspective this is not very nice that Bolt drivers use stolen cars. This can lead to media scandal.
Thus, I would recommend to ask [@serhii.pavlyk|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UF4NTL3SL] what’s his decision in light of the fact that under the law we are under no obligation to report it or terminate the driver. However,  we can terminate / report them if respective business decision is taken.

(
	select ic.external_id, ic.type, ebrb.client_id, ebrb.sum_with_vat, ebrb.currency, ebrb.subtype, ebrb.date
	from etl_billing_rides_balance ebrb

	where ic.country = 'tn' and ic.type in ('Driver', 'Company')
),
month_end_balance as 
(
	select td.external_id, td.type, td.client_id, td.currency, sum(sum_with_vat) as month_end_balance
	from tunisia_drivers td
	where td.date < date('2022-07-01')
	group by 1, 2, 3, 4
	having month_end_balance < 0
),
collection_after_cutoff as 
(
	select td.external_id, td.type, td.client_id, td.currency, sum(case when sum_with_vat > 0 then sum_with_vat end) as positive_balance_after
	from tunisia_drivers td
	where td.date >= date('2022-07-01')
	group by 1, 2, 3, 4
)
select 
ic."name",
coalesce(fd.company_name, fc."name", fc2."name") as company_name,
coalesce(fd.company_id, fc.id) as company_id,
meb.*, 
--cac.positive_balance_after, 
least(-meb.month_end_balance, coalesce(cac.positive_balance_after, 0)) as collection_of_meb, 
-collection_of_meb/meb.month_end_balance as collection_rate
from month_end_balance meb
left join collection_after_cutoff cac on cac.client_id = meb.client_id and cac.currency = meb.currency 
left join fleet_driver fd on fd.id = meb.external_id and meb.type = 'Driver'
left join fleet_company fc on fc.id = meb.external_id and meb.type = 'Company'

I think I need this improvement (actually not the complete improvement but a small part of it in the context of price surging).

Context (with 2 possible issues in my current project):

* when /placeOrder is called and the price has changed we will return {{MENU_HAS_CHANGED}} error. We return this because UI knows how to handle the error code: it will do a /getCheckoutSummary and this endpoint’s response will return a basket alert. This alert will tell the user that the price has changed and it will save that price on the DB. After this, when /placeOrder is called again then the call will succeed.
** issue:
*** {{MENU_HAS_CHANGED}} because it is not sent with a proper message (just plain error) → UI notice this and shows a default message
*** getCheckoutSummary is called again and another error (this time with the proper message) is shown
*** => two errors will pop and user might be a bit confused (however, the first error message will be seen for a short period of time so user might not even notice
* let’s assume that on /getCheckoutSummary we notice that the delivery price has changed → we will show user a basket alert
** issue:
*** UI doesn’t know to refetch provider details (the new price on the provider page → user will see the old price)

Solution:

Firstly let’s try to define what actions UI will do after the user will press the alert button.

Let’s consider the following interface

{noformat} export interface BasketAlertButton {
     text: LocalisedString;
+    /*
+     * deprecated with certain app version
+     *
+     */
     action?: BasketAlertButtonAction;
+    /*
+     * array of actions
+     * if ui_actions.length > 0 => UI can perform each UIActions in parallel 
+     * (tbd about race conditions deadlocks & stuff t)
+     * */
+    ui_actions?: UIActions[];
+}
+
+export interface UIActions {
+    /*
+     * a list of actions that will be serially executed on UI
+     * */
+    action_list: Action[];
+}
+
+export interface Action {
+    /*
+     * each action will have a result
+     * if the action failed and if this is skippable then UI can proceed to the next action
+     * in case of failure some logging should be done (perhaps on UI side)
+     * */
+    skippable: boolean; 
+    /*
+     * This defines some actions that UI can perform
+     * */
+    type: ActionType;
+}
+
+export enum ActionType {
+    REFETCH_CHECKOUT_SUMMARY = "refetch_checkout_summary",
+    REFETCH_PROVIDER_DETAILS = "refetch_provider_details",
+    REFETCH_PROVIDER_MENU = "refetch_provider_menu",
+    DELETE_BASKET = "delete_basket"
 }{noformat}



We can also extend the following interface:

{noformat} export interface ValidationErrorResponseData extends ErrorResponseData {
+    /*
+     * todo: does something break on UI if this is field is optional
+     * */
+    alert?: BasketAlert;
+    /*these actions will be executed when UI receives that error*/
+    ui_actions?: UIActions[];{noformat}

In this case those UI actions will be executed when the UI will receive the error (even before showing the basket alert) (we can also define here actions that can be done in background so that UI can show the alert if such field exists).





How does this solve my problems?

* for the first example, we can throw an error with a simple action called \[{{DONT_SHOW_ANY_ERROR}} , {{REFETCH_CHECKOUT_SUMMARY}}] 
* for the second example we can have the following action type on the ok button \[{{REFETCH_PROVIDER_DETAILS}}]

I’d say that UI should focus only on those 3 actions only and only for checkoutSummary and placeOrder endpoints.

Hi [~accountid:5ed5e92f88deed0c1803081c], 

I have done a standard red flag review of this since it had already been reviewed before but to my surprise the agreement does not include our standard requests for agreements as per the below: 

* *Clause 2 - Termination for convenience for Bolt is crucial:* Things change fast at Bolt\! Thus, Bolt should have the right to terminate the contract for convenience, ideally by notifying the other party not more than 30-90 days in advance. If having a right to terminate for convenience becomes an issue in negotiations, the reasonable middle ground may be to include a minimum initial term as is the case here (1 year), before which a party cannot exercise the right to terminate for convenience. After the initial 1 year period, Bolt should be able to terminate for convenience by giving written notice. The current wording locks in Bolt for a 1 year period each time without a right to termination. This is generally against our internal guidelines but given that this has already been confirmed by us and Ruter - can you confirm that you are fine with the risk of not being able to terminate this other than at the end och each 1 year period? 
* *No further fees*: Termination should result in no further fees being owed by Bolt nor should Bolt be financially penalised for terminating the contract early. Further, if Bolt has made any advance payments, these must be repaid on a pro-rata basis. Currently no such wording is included in the agreement. 
* *Clause 8.3 - Remedy of breach*: Each Party shall have the right to terminate the contract if the other party has not remedied the breach within 30 days. 
* *Clause 8.5 - Immediate termination*: need to include the termination right if the other party becomes insolvent etc. 
* *Clause 11.1* - *Confidentiality*: the included clause is insufficient. Confidentiality clauses are of high importance for Bolt in order to keep any business secrets and insufficient clauses may have damaging consequences in terms of products releases or investor issues. The current clause lacks a definition of what "Confidential Information" is covered, does not clearly state when information may be shared and does not state that the clause will be valid for 3 years post termination of the agreement (survival period). These are standards that we must include in each agreement. 
* *Notices clause*:  the agreement does not include a clear notices clause. We need to include a clear notices clause which allows Bolt to send notices via email. This is necessary in order to avoid any discussions or disagreements on whether notice has been given in compliance with the agreement. 
* *Appendix to 6 - Privacy review:* this must be reviewed by our privacy team - have you involved them in this? Otherwise, we need to do so as soon as possible.

Testable UX at moment of writing:

* Added business expense note text input to checkout screen - it is shown only if a business payment method with ask_user_note = true is selected for the basket.

* An error message is displayed if the required input is missing. If both courier note and expense note are missing when trying to place the order, both inputs become red but the focus is set on courier note.
* The expense note value is sent to the API, -which has a bug that needs to be solved by payments team, not sure when you will be able to test the full integration and view the saved expense note in the DB-.

h3. *🇩🇪 Germany*

*🚗  Ride hailing*

*Important:* As mentioned above, requests from authorities are handled by Tier 2 in Germany. However, the flow is the following:

* Tier 2 handles the request and responds to the police
* Tier 2 fills out the Event Assessment Tool
* Once the previous steps are done, Tier 2 should choose the safety severity level of the ticket:
** Minor: insurance issues
** Severe: all other police requests
* After changing the severity level, the ticket should be escalated to the International CS Safety team by changing the tier to Safety

*Note:* If you’re an RH agent and come across a police request for Micromobility, change the user persona from _Authority_ to _Scooter/E-bike rider_. This way, the ticket will be sent to the relevant queue.

🛴 *Micromobility*

Police requests are handled by both Tier 1 and Tier 2. The workflow is the following:

* The tier should be changed to _Tier 1_. Tier 1 will fill out the tool and add the translation of the message to the internal notes.
* Once done, Tier 1 should change the tier to _Tier 2_
* Tier 2 agent will take the ticket and respond to the police
* Once the request has been handled, the user persona should be changed back to _Authority._

I checked the following cases: 

Case 1: there is a physical assault threat (the driver threatened to hit a person in the head) and the case needs investigation as per SOP. However, a 4 days turnaround time is way too high and this is mainly a CS Safety backlog issue. 

Case 2: In Lithuania, there is vehicle’s pic instead of driver’s pic. If the vehicle matches with the one in-app (and not with the pic), then it’s not a safety case. This can be reminded to agents and if necessary I can add a note to the SOP. I understand the situation might have created confusion. 

Case 3: Contacting the passenger for any other reason than lost items is not allowed. [~accountid:5d0c8f1621a5d30bc4e096a8] I was thinking about whether we should slightly change this EC and make it a regular event. If on the phone there is any other issue (like inappropriate behaviour or a threat), then we can use different ECs. I understand the concern here, for this case a block is not justified in my opinion. 

Case 4: Should touting be a UK-specific EC? I don’t think it should be treated differently than asking for more money in other markets unless there is a reg.  requirement. 

Case 5: The case definitely needed investigation, but the turnaround time is not very good. 

Case 6: It’s correct to investigate, but the escalation (9 days) took too long. 

Case 7: Asking the driver to go provide medical records is a no for me. About the calling part, it cannot be done by CS Safety, but maybe CS teams can call instead of translating written messages? This should be asked to the CS Safety team.  

Case 8: I can’t open it. 



However the main points here: 

* Investigating more on the driver - rating, amount of trips, and previous comments. 

I agree they should be checked, but a clean rating does not mean any offense. 

* Not blocking the drivers without a final decision or keeping a stricter and shorter case-solving time.

Definitely keep blocking for significant events but the case-solving time it too long right now. 

* Contact the drivers via phone and hear both sides of the story before making suspension.

This could potentially be done by local teams if they agree to do it, but not by CS Safety. 

* Decisions are made only based on one ticket, which could possibly be a false report just to receive a promo code. 

We can’t assume that a report is false or that a party is lying.

We have reviewed and analyzed the documentation you provided to us and you will find below the outcome of our analysis:

# +Assessing whether the selfies would constitute biometric data+

As you certainly know, the GDPR (and French law) defines “biometric data” as “personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person, which allow or confirm the unique identification of that natural person, such as facial images or dactyloscopic data”.

The GDPR adopts a functional approach: biometric data is data used to identify a person. The GDPR is technology neutral: whatever the technical process used to process the data, it only focusses on the goal: identifying a person.

The French data protection authority (CNIL) published a [detailed analysis of the CNIL on facial recognition|https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/atoms/files/reconnaissance_faciale.pdf] in 2019 defining facial recognition as “_a computational and probabilistic technique that automatically recognises a person on the basis of their face, to authenticate or identify them_”. The CNIL categorizes facial recognition in “_the broader category of biometric techniques_”, with an identification function that “_aims to find a person within a group of individuals, in a place, an image or a database_”.

That being said, a mere image or picture does not constitute in itself a biometric data. This is confirmed both by the 2019 CNIL analysis (and subsequent CNIL websties guidance) and by the recitals of the GDPR which states that: “_The processing of photographs should not systematically be considered to be processing of special categories of personal data as they are covered by the definition of biometric data only when processed through a specific technical means allowing the unique identification or authentication of a natural person_ (GDPT lit. 51)”.

So, in our opinion, the mere fact for drivers to take a selfie and/or for Bolt to store a previous image/picture of the driver (without further processing on this image) does not constitute a biometric data at this stage.

However, a facial recognition system implies that data subject’s photographs must be processed specifically to extract biometric data. The CNIL published guidelines and explanations on how these facial recognition systems works and we assume that Bolt is using similar verification systems: for the CNIL, recognition can be performed from still images (photos) or moving images (video recordings) and takes place in two phases:

* From the image, a model or "template" (

_gabarit_) that represents, from a computer point of view, the characteristics of the face is created. The data extracted to constitute this template are biometric data within the meaning of the GDPR (article 4-14).

* The recognition phase is then carried out by comparing these previously made templates with the templates calculated live on faces present on the candidate image.

In the case of identification, the system checks whether the face model presented matches one of the models in the database. The results of the comparison correspond to the one or ones with the highest similarity score among those exceeding a certain predetermined threshold.

Our understanding of the section “how it works” section of the Bolts’s Driver Selfie Checks document is that is it exactly what Bolt is doing, so this verification process of Selfie triggers the processing of biometric data.

*CNIL’s STANDARD REGULATION FOR BIOMETRIC SYSTEMS IN THE WORKPLACE:*

In accordance with Article 9 (4) of the GDPR, which provides that “_Member States may maintain or introduce further conditions, including limitations, with regard to the processing of genetic data, biometric data or data concerning health_“, the revised French data protection act 78-17 of 6 January 1978  granted the CNIL the power to issue “_standard regulations to ensure the security of personal data processing systems and to regulate the processing of genetic data, biometric data and health data_”.

Based on such power, the CNIL adopted on 10 January 2019, its first [standard regulation|https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/atoms/files/deliberation-2019-001-10-01-2019-reglement-type-controle-dacces-biometrique.pdf] that lays down legally binding rules applicable to data controllers subject to French Law, who use biometric systems to control access to premises, devices and applications at work (the “*Regulation*“).

The Regulation imposes specific requirements and conditions for the processing, by a public or private employer, of biometric data to control accesses to work premises, to information systems or applications used in the context of business tasks entrusted to data subjects (i.e., employees, agents, interns and contractors). Thus, although this Regulation is mainly designed to apply in an employer – employee context, it also applies to contractors (so Bolt drivers would fall under the scope of this Regulation). It concerns the access to limitatively identified devices or apps used by the controller (here, this would be the Bolt’s platform).

The CNIL reminds that the rules and conditions resulting from the Regulation do not exclude the application of the general obligations under the GDPR, notably regarding compliance with the general principles for processing personal data. To be transparent, there is a slightly grey area on whether this Regulation satisfies the requirements of article 9.2.(g). The Regulation only states that the controller must document an appropriate legal basis under article 6 of the GDPR and in a FAQ published by the CNIL on this Regulation, the CNIL does not mention article 9 but only stress on the obligation to justify the need for the data controller to use a biometric system and that there is no less intrusive means (badges or access code) to satisfy the purposes. The CNIL also recommends to avoid using consent as a legal basis in the employment context and suggest to rely on the legitimate interest instead. Our understanding is thus that a data controller that strictly complies with the Regulations requirements will be able to implement a biometric systems, without having to rely on a legal basis provided in article 9.2.

This Regulation is quite long and lays out stringent obligations to data controllers regarding the conditions of processing of such biometric data in the workplace which and you will find an high-level summary below:

·       *Limited purposes*: the purposes of the processing are strictly limited to access control of premises requiring restricted access or access control to a limited number of devices and IT professional applications, which must be clearly identified by the organization.

·       *Proportionality*: the organization must demonstrate that it is not possible to achieve the above purposes by means other than the processing of biometric data. The data controller must document why such a high level of protection is needed given the context at hand and evidence why the processing of biometric data is the most relevant mean to ensure security.

·       *Data Minimization* must be taken into account;

·       *Restricted access to the data*: internal “authorisation profiles” must be implemented to access biometric data. Only the personnel having legitimate business needs, depending on their function, may access biometric data (accesses differ depending on the personnel collecting the biometric data) ;

·       *Restrictions applicable to biometric data*: only biometric authentication based on morphological characteristics of data subjects may be used and the biometric mean selected (e.g., use of iris recognition rather than fingerprints) must be documented and justified.

·       *Types of biometric templates:* for the purpose of the Regulation, a template is a set of measurements of an individual’s morphological characteristics. The Regulation defines three template types which correspond to various levels of data subject control over the way their biometric data is processed by the employer:

·       “*Type 1*” template is the most protective of individual rights: it is stored on a medium which remains under the individual’s exclusive possession (e.g., token or badge) .

·       “*Type 2*” template is under the shared control between the individual and the employer: there is a centralized template database which is encrypted and may only be activated under the control of the individual at hand.

·       “*Type 3*” template is under the exclusive control of the employer and creates the highest risks for individual privacy in the event of a data breach as there is a centralized template database.

The Regulation specifies that “Type 1” template must be used as a matter of principle, whereas “Type 2” and “Type 3” (which we understand will be the one used by BOLT) templates shall only be used *under exceptional and justified circumstances where type 1 or 2 would not be adequate*

·       *Limited retention*: the raw records (photo, audio recording, etc.) of the biometric feature can only be processed for the time necessary to calculate the template:  they cannot be stored. Derived biometric data can only be stored in the form of encrypted templates that do not allow the original biometric characteristic to be recalculated. They must be deleted in the event of withdrawal of the authorizations or in the event of the person concerned ceases to work for the employing organization. Log data and identification data shall be retained for 6 months further to the recording thereof – but may be kept in archive mode if required by law of for contentious purpose in compliance with the applicable statute of limitation.

·       *Data Subject Information*: data subject must be provided with specific and individual information prior to the time of enrolment of their biometric characteristics in the system.

·       *Security measures*: the data controller must take any useful precautions, taking in consideration the nature of the data and the risks raised by the processing for data subjects and their rights, to preserve the availability, integrity and confidentiality of the data. The Regulation includes a long list of security measures.

·       *Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA)*: The data controller must conduct a DPIA.

Hey [~accountid:60950a25539c14006ae92e40] 

# We can create a low prio task for the single char timeout. So long as the input still works, and providers can be located with narrower query strings, there is not much of a problem. To fully resolve, we’d need some kind of page-walking logic for the backend filtering call, which would not be too hard, but the benefit-effort ratio doesn’t warrant a higher prio task. Another option would probably be prefix searches, as it seems like the API filters records using a “contains”-filter. Third option, as suggested by you, is to wait for at least two characters to be provided before we send off the API request. This is probably the best option.
# Unfortunately the API endpoint we use does not support fuzzy querying. So if we remove the full id match logic (applied when the query string is a number), then you will not be able to find providers by just providing their id. This could be a trivial prio task, as I’m not sure Lifecycle would see the need to add support for such queries.

To put number 2 simpler: the API has two fields for filtering ({{provider_name}} and {{id}}), so either we make two calls for every applicable query, or we do something “smart” like switching to the {{id}} field if the query is an integer, which is what we do at the moment. The superior alternative is something like a {{provider_name_or_id}} field that would merge results for both filter types, but I’m not sure how it will be welcomed (and the benefits offered are probably not worth the effort).

[~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] asked the DPO Team to provide specific questions related to the Ghana verification process and to express the main concerns about the incident. First of all, I would like to state explicitly that these questions are not intended to criticize anyone, but to find a solution. An attempt is also made to raise questions that could be asked by a supervisory authority):

1.) Is the current verification process happening as described in the ticket? (Transmission of a driver's license picture and another picture that shows the same person)
1a)  If not, what is the process like?
1b) Are there additional tools to prevent fraud or identity fraud?
1c) Did this type of driver verification process represent the state of the art at the time of the implementation?

2.) Since when has the verification process been done in this way in Ghana?
2a) Was a DPIA carried out in advance? Was there a legal review?
2b) Have the issues of fraud and identity theft been addressed during implementation?
2c) How many drivers were added to the platform in this way in Ghana?
2d) Besides this case, are there other known cases of identity fraud?
2e) Are there accompanying measures that confirm the authenticity of the drivers?

3) Referring to [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3964829758/Driver+Selfie+Checks#Eligibility-and-country-specifics|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3964829758/Driver+Selfie+Checks#Eligibility-and-country-specifics|smart-link], what measures can be taken to better verify the identity of drivers in the short/medium/long term when they are added to the app?
3a) What are possible solutions to mitigate the risk? What measures are there to confirm the identity of the current drivers, who have already verified themselves by submitting 2 pictures, on the platform?

4.) Which countries are also affected?

*Major concerns:*
1.) In Ghana a data controller who processes personal data shall ensure that the data is complete, accurate, up to date. *The current process includes the huge risk of getting inaccurate data* (I know that we have in our TnCs that drivers have to provide accurate data, but this does not relieve us from the obligation to take appropriate steps to secure the integrity of personal data).

2.) There is also a *risk (as in this case) that incorrect information will be disclosed* (this is not about the disclosure of the photo per se, but about the disclosure of a photo of an uninvolved third party in combination with the fact that this uninvolved third party provides cab-services). This can (but doesn't have to) lead to personal insecurity ("Am I affected by identity theft?") or humiliation ("My friends/business partners think that I'm doing so bad financially that I'm a part-time taxi driver").

3) The Data Protection Act in Ghana requires that a data controller shall take the necessary steps to secure the integrity of personal data in the possession or control of a person through the adoption of appropriate, reasonable, technical and organisational measures to prevent loss of, damage to, or unauthorised destruction; and unlawful access to or unauthorised processing of personal data. The Act requires that to give effect to this, the data controller must take reasonable measures to
·       identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to personal data under that person's possession or control;
·       establish and maintain appropriate safeguards against the identified risks;
·       regularly verify that the safeguards are effectively implemented; and
·       ensure that the safeguards are continually updated in response to new risks or deficiencies.

*This case can lead to the supervisory authority assuming that the controller has not taken sufficient measures in this area.*

4) *Exkurs:* Apart from data protection considerations, the fact that services are provided on the platform by drivers, who are using the identity of an uninvolved third party, can also lead to significant security concerns. This can make it more difficult for the company to implement additional security features and also contains a risk for the company's reputation.

[~accountid:5da0457ac7706e0dc0698d7e] thanks for confirming\! 

As a general rule, deposits are not within the scope of VAT (i.e. no need to issue a VAT invoice for the same). However, in case the tablets are not returned by providers, such that we adjust our inventory and balance sheet accordingly, we must charge VAT on the supply. At this point, Bolt Operations OU (i.e. the group company that has the relationship with the provider, other than UA and AZ where the relationship is between the local entity and providers) must generate an invoice to the provider and charge local VAT (usually standard rate applies) on the “sale”. 

There should not be any adverse corporation tax consequences arising from the implementation of deposits, or the subsequent sale of the tablets provided that the sales price of the tables to providers is not higher than the original purchase price of the assets for Bolt. 

To sum up, from a tax perspective, there should not be any showstoppers relating to the implementation of deposits on tablets. However, please confirm the process for the same - especially as regards non-returned tablets - with the finance & commerce teams before implementing such deposits.

[~accountid:620faeb2eb2978006893882d], as for any debt of the couriers/fleets owed to us, the General Terms with the Couriers (clause 8.3) include the following provision:

“_8.3.  Bolt undertakes to forward all Courier Fee and (where applicable) the Small Order Fee payments from the Client to the Courier’s bank account that was provided to Bolt by Courier, except for cash payments (unless the Client fails to pay Courier Fee and (where applicable) the Small Order Fee to the Courier)._ *_No payments shall be made if the amount payable to Couriers for the reference period falls below the minimum payment threshold established by Bolt or in case the Balance is negative after the reference period. In the event that the Courier has to pay Agency Fee to Bolt under Section 7.5 of these General Terms, Bolt shall prepare and issue a VAT invoice to the Courier for the Agency Fee (if necessary) and deduct the Agency Fee from the payment made to the Courier._*”

This means that if after the referencing period (one week) we see that the fleet has negative balance, we are entitled to suspend all payments to them and deduct the amount owed by the fleet to Bolt from the amount owed by Bolt to the fleet.

Further, clause 9.1 of the General Terms provides:

“_9.1.  If the Courier breaches any of the obligations set out in these General Terms, any applicable laws or regulations, disparage Bolt, or cause harm to Bolt’s brand, reputation or business as determined by Bolt in its own sole discretion, or Bolt has reasonable belief of fraudulent acts by the Courier when using the Bolt Food Platform,_ *_Bolt has the right to temporarily suspend the Courier from using the Bolt Food Platform or terminate this Agreement without any obligation to compensate for the loss of profit._* _In the aforementioned cases Bolt may, in its own discretion, prohibit the Courier from registering a new Courier account._“

Hence, in our case we are entitled to do either or all of the following:

1. Stop all payments to the fleet;

2. Deduct from the payout due to the fleet the amount owed by them to Bolt;

3. Suspend this fleet from the platform;

4. Terminate the agreement immediately.

As for the situation with their couriers, it is more of a matter that we could try to resolve in the negotiations with the fleet. I would advise to have the meeting with them as planned and discuss this issue. 

Since we have some evidence of their fraud and misconduct, we can mention this and say that either the fleet immediately ceases to carry out these actions and repays the debt owed to us, or we will be forced to resort to the judicial way of resolution of this matter.

Hi Edna, 
Thanks for reporting this issue. 
Car rental is the only exception for the credit limit. For car rentals, one order can consist of many “suborders” (of value max 50€). The thing is though, that for car rentals *we check if the credit limit is violated only when making the first order*. And in that case, it wasn’t. Subsequent suborders within that order are not checked. The reasoning behind that logic was that some suborders may happen automatically (50€ limit is reached), let’s say when the user is driving 120km/h on a highway. We wouldn’t like to stop the user in such cases and deny them the service. But this comes with a price, as we see now - so the businesses can exceed their limits significantly.

As for preventing this from happening, we are currently working on a soluion.

Hello,

You’re entirely correct. It’s explicit in Article 39(1)(c) that the DPO must “provide advice where requested as regards the data protection impact assessment and monitor its performance.” This task is included what you correctly mentioned from WP243.

However, to indicate which safeguards should be applied to mitigate the risks, it’s necessary to know:

# What is the process as a whole: what data will be collected; why data will be collected; from where data will be collected; when data will be collected; who will collect the data; and how data will be collected. *These aspects were not indicated in the DPIA*.
# What is the legal basis defined by the controller to support this data processing activity. *This was not indicated in the DPIA*.
# What risks the controller see in the data processing activity. *This was not completely indicated in the DPIA*.

This is also present in Article 35(7) GDPR, which states that the DPIA “shall contain at least:

* (a) a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued by the controller;
* (b) an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes;
* (c) an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects referred to in paragraph 1; and
* (d) the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of personal data and to demonstrate compliance with this Regulation taking into account the rights and legitimate interests of data subjects and other persons concerned.”

*Without such information, it is impossible to indicate any kind of mitigation measure*.

We cannot indicate a measure to mitigate risks if the risks have not been pointed out, and the risks are pointed out from the process as a whole. In the specific case of this DPIA, and *just as an example*, if the data is collected to check if the driver has exceeded the speed limit and this data is automatically deleted after collection, we probably will have a low risk. But if the data is stored and used to define a possible driver profile over time, we have a higher risk than in the previous situation. In other words, without knowing the process as a whole, it is impossible to determine the level of risk and consequently impossible to indicate any risk mitigation measures.

This is why we requested more information so that the DPO Team could recommend these measures.

This DPIA *will be our priority* as soon as we receive the information requested. If you need anything else, please let us know.

Host in {{/etc/mysql/alters.agent.prelive.cnf}} should be the hostname of prelive of {{RENTAL-CENTRAL}}, the same one that you use to connect when you’re performing native apply in prelive.

This file should be placed on the master host of {{RENTAL-CENTRAL}}, which is {{rencen-d1.sqldb}} currently.

Below is some general information explaining the mechanism of native apply on prelive in Alter Automation.

----

Once Alter Orchestrator asks Supervisor to perform native apply, Supervisor will query DB Topology service (which queries MySQL Orchestrator) to find the master host of the given cluster. Then Supervisor asks the Agent on the master host to perform native apply *in prelive specifically*. Seeing that this is a request for native apply in prelive, Agent will use {{/etc/mysql/alters.agent.prelive.cnf}} config file to initialize a MySQL connection to an actual prelive DB and will apply the DDL there.

Why is the config on master? Ideally we would put an agent on prelive and the config would be there. However, as you mentioned, it’s not that easy to install an Agent on an LXD container, hence the workaround with master and prelive config. We have agreed on this workaround with [~accountid:6012c28a3b1af00069a0c0a7] previously. We have exact same setup in staging (prelive config on master host) and it proved to be working.

*Summary:* Bolt is obligated to comply with the request according to Section 47 (5) of The Personal Income Tax Act, (on which the request of CRIRS is based), which mandates all organisations to provide all requested information to a tax authority, upon demand. Therefore, Bolt has the obligation to provide the requested information to CRIRS. 

However, Bolt should still adhere to the principle of data minimisation and provide only the information necessary to achieve the purpose. 

After Slack discussion with Nnaemeka the decision was to provide in first instance only data on existing drivers as at the end of 2021. The following data categories would be provided:

* driver name
* phone number

If further information is required, the request can be assessed again. 

In addition,  under the Guidelines for the Management of Personal Data by Public Institutions in Nigeria, 2020 (the “Guidelines”), where a public institution requests for personal data from a data controller, the data controller is required to submit a report the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA)1 prior to sending the personal information to the public institution. Bolt will, therefore, be required to submit a report of the requested details to the NITDA, prior to sending the personal information to the CRIRS.

The regulations around this in Finland stipulate the following:

* *Fixed Term Contracts*: An employment contract in Finland is valid indefinitely unless it has, for a justified reason, been made for a specific fixed term. If the employer want to enter into a fixed term contract it needs to be established on what basis the contract is fixed and not until further notice. Example for justified reason is that the business only requires additional workers for a certain period of time due to changes in demand.
* *Hour limits*: Employment contracts in Finland can be entered into on a full-time or part-time basis. Full-time work entails a regular working time which may not exceed eight hours per day and 40 hours per week. Part-time work is any system of working time that falls short of full-time work. There is no specific limit on the number of hours that such part-time work needs to meet.
* *Flexibility*: The employer and employee can agree on a fixed number of minimum working hours with the option to add more working hours but if the hours are up to 40 this will then be classified as full time work and not a part-time contract. The average weekly working hours may not exceed 40 regardless if classified as part-time or full-time work.
* *Benefits*: The benefits in part-time work may not be less favourable than those of full-time employees merely because the employee is working on a part-time basis, but they may be proportioned to the working time.

This only covers the legal review and not the HR policy which should be done by HR.

*Art 31 Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) - Notification of security compromises*

*Notification of security compromises*
31. (1) Where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the personal data of a data subject has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, the data controller or a third party who processes data under the authority of the data controller shall notify the

(a) Commission, and

(b) the data subject

of the unauthorised access or acquisition.

(2) The notification shall be made as soon as reasonably practicable after the discovery of the unauthorised access or acquisition of the data.

(3) The data controller shall take steps to ensure the restoration of the integrity of the information system.

(4) The data controller shall delay notification to the data subject where the security agencies or the Commission inform the data controller that notification will impede a criminal investigation.

(5) The notification to a data subject shall be communicated by

(a) registered mail to the last known residential or postal address of the data subject;(b) electronicmailtothelastknownelectronicmailaddressofthe data subject;(c) placement in a prominent position on the website of the responsible party;(d) publication in the media; or(e) any other manner that the Commission may direct.

(6) A notification shall provide sufficient information to allow the data subject to take protective measures against the consequences of unauthorised access or acquisition of the data.

(7) The information shall include, if known to the data controller, the identity of the unauthorised person who may have accessed or acquired the personal data.

(8) Where the Commission has grounds to believe that publicity would  protect a data subject who is affected by the unauthorised access or acquisition of data, the Commission may direct the data controller to publicise in the specified manner, the fact of the compromise to the integrity or confidentiality of the personal data.

Based on these slack-threads ([1|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01VCDMA8K0/p1663161114791629] & [2|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CNV6QPRFT/p1663153576832069]) and code-analysis the following conclusions can be reached:

* There is an ongoing migration effort in which Payment Methods are going to be replaced by [Payment Instruments|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3503326314/Payment+Instrument]: 
{noformat}Payment Methods
payment_method_type: adyen|zooz|processout|adyen_paypal
payment_method_id: some_unique_reference_to_external_system
Sample: type=adyen_paypal & id=2916267837698724

Payment Instruments
payment_instrument_id: string
For backwards compatibility purposes, it is currently constructed as a concatenation of type&id
Sample: id=adyen_paypal/2916267837698724{noformat}
* On delivery side, this migration is not completed yet, as for other verticals; There are [some proposed solutions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3804397661/Payment+method+in+API+WIP] for how this will be happening, but no final decision has been taken yet 
* Our project is dependent on *balance-team,* since we take the payment method info from two endpoints that they own:
** {{/internal/v1/delivery/getPaymenet}}  from {{commerce-gateway}}
** {{internal/getBooking}} from balance-user → which is deprecated and should be removed 
* From my perspective, this migration should not affect our efforts in a significant way, because, the main difference from the actual implementation is the fact that for *Payment Instruments*, payment method id & type will be concatenated together in an ID string. As per payment-team, this change aims to make the intermediary card payment processor opaque to the endpoint clients (meaning that we would not be able to distinguish between {color:#97a0af}adyen / processout / zooz / paystack {color}). However, all the other sub-types: card, cash, mobile_money, bolt_credit, paypal, ideal will still be available. Moreover, even the payment processor should be available, since, for backwards compatibility the name will be part of the *Payment Instrument ID* , and it seems that [balance-team proposal|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3804397661/Payment+method+in+API+WIP] also counts on this info. 

My conclusion is that the payment method subtype should be stored as a string(VARCHAR) in DB, and we should not be concerned if at some-point the payment-processor type will no longer be available to us, and we will store “card” instead, as the same issue should happen to basket team also, and {{CHECKOUT_COMPLETE}} events should still be easily matched. 



PS:  Basked on a DM with Tudor from Basket, they also use Payment Methods(with a single instance where they use payment instruments but there they split the ID into type/name ) and also are dependent on commerce-gateway moving from Payment Methods to Payment Instruments).

* As long as alcohol products are sold by the seller to the client directly (in terms of legal contract and in terms of invoicing – see below with respect to invoices on behalf of the seller by Bolt), Bolt would avoid licensing regime that is generally applicable to the sellers and to the sale of alcohol products.

* In such model, the sellers of alcohol products normally would remain liable for any non-compliance with age, time and other regulatory requirements up until the moment of delivery to the client. Therefore, Bolt should expect that the sellers may require Bolt to offer certain contractual assurances.

* Invoices for alcohol products may be be issued on behalf of the sellers by Bolt, but Bolt should have in mind that such intermediation for invoicing purposes is not particularly welcomed by the authority (the authority normally wants to see direct invoicing by the seller to the client). Such intermediation however is applied by the current market players; thus, this poses rather low practical risk.

* The delivery of alcohol products as such does not require a license. The couriers however may need to update their food registrations by including alcohol products into the range of products they are delivering (those who have not done so already). The couriers of course would also be subject to age, time and certain other restrictions.

* As mentioned, the sale and delivery of alcohol products is subject to age, time and certain other requirements, the list of which we are ready to provide if needed.

At this point we are not able to provide the data in the way envisaged for the following reason:

# It is not clear *what would be the legal basis for data sharing* with the authority. Article 2.2 of the NDPR provides possible lawful bases which includes the lawful basis of a legal obligation. Article 2.2(c) of the NDPR states: Without prejudice to the principles set out in this Regulation (the NDPR), processing shall be lawful if at least one of the following applies: … (c) processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the Controller is subject. 

No legal obligation stemming from the law has been presented under which we are obliged to provide such data. 
# Data protection principles such as purposefulness and data minimisation are not followed (even if there would exist a legal basis under law). As a rule, data should be processed (including disclosed) only to achieve the specific purpose and following the data minimisation principle. 

Providing personal data on both drivers and passengers proactively to the authority without any specific safety or security incident related to these individuals is excessive from privacy viewpoint. 

Please let me know if there are some further arguments raised by the airport authority and when they can present the legal basis on which this data transfer would be based upon.

*1. Collecting data by Bolt*

If Bolt would be the entity to initially collect data and set up the accounts with Awin, it would make Bolt a data controller in this capacity. This means that Bolt would have to deliver on its own notification requirements as set our in the data protection legislation. Please see the draft here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/14zH0HaL_weRrWnuu8vKLTCZnCZ6qhrDznjTLPH7mmDM/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/14zH0HaL_weRrWnuu8vKLTCZnCZ6qhrDznjTLPH7mmDM/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link]  . Please note that we don’t need end user’s acceptance (for example in the form of a check box) - we simply have to present it, by - for example-  linking it in the form. Disclaimer with the following wording included in the form would be sufficient:

_Your personal data will be processed by Bolt Operations OÜ as a data controller in accordance with the Privacy Notice \[link]._

*_Can we immediately delete all data after accomplishing the object of the processing of the respective data, e.g rides data after each ride, User data after removing the User from Team Account, or all Customer related data after terminating the Agreement?_*

_Bolt processes personal data as described in_ [_Bolt’s Privacy Notice_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/privacy-for-riders/] _for Passengers and Riders. The retention terms of the data is described in clause 7 of the Privacy Notice. As a general rule, personal data will be stored as long as there is an active account. If the account is closed, personal data will be deleted (according to our retention schedule and rules), unless such data is still required to meet any legal obligation, or for accounting, dispute resolution or fraud prevention purposes._

_As there has been a contractual relationship, data may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from the agreement. Deleting all the data deprives us from the opportunity to evidence the fulfilment of our obligations under the agreement in the event that any claims should arise. Therefore the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller until the term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims)._

_When the Customer’s account has been deactivated, the the data which we hold will and can only be used to meet legal obligations, accounting and dispute resolution purposes. Confidentiality and security of the data is guaranteed throughout the storage period._

Hey.. again 😄 

So to have the guidelines correct once and for all and to avoid future confusion, I’ve added them to the police requests process (updates not published yet) as this is the process CS will look at when handling police tickets. Once it’s published, I’ll also link it to the Escalation guidelines. 

But to avoid confusion, I think we should make it clear for all business lines. Please see the guidelines here:

h3. *🚗 Ride-hailing*

*Markets with a dedicated CS Safety team*

Click _Edit case data_ and change the tier to _Safety_ and the severity level to _Minor_. The ticket will be taken over by CS Safety. - {color:#36b37e}*Which safety severity level CS Safety should use? It is Minor by default as it’s being escalated from a non-safety agent, but should they change it at some point?*{color}

*Markets without a dedicated CS Safety team*

The flow is the following:

* Tier 2 handles the request and responds to the police
* Tier 2 fills out the Event Assessment Tool
* Once the previous steps are done, Tier 2 should choose the safety severity level of the ticket:
** *Minor*: insurance issues
** *Severe*: all other police requests
* After changing the severity level, the ticket should be escalated to the International CS Safety team by changing the tier to Safety

*Note:* If you’re an RH agent and come across a police request for Micromobility, change the user persona from _Authority_ to _Scooter/E-bike rider_. This way, the ticket will be sent to the relevant queue.

----

h3. 🛴 *Micromobility -* {color:#36b37e}*this is clear I believe*{color}

Police requests are handled by both Tier 1 and Tier 2. The workflow is the following:

* The tier should be changed to _Tier 1_ and the user persona to _Scooter/E-bike rider_. Tier 1 will fill out the tool and add the translation of the message to the internal notes.
* Once done, Tier 1 should change the tier to _Tier 2_ (with the user persona still _Scooter/E-bike rider_).
* Tier 2 agent will take the ticket and respond to the police
* Once the request has been handled, the user persona should be changed back to _Authority._

----

Hi Matilda, 

Regarding compensation to Bolt balance, we have had a few customers send a screenshot of this [FAQ article |https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360021473640-I-want-to-check-my-refund-status]which says *Refunds on the platform can be issued to your Bolt balance or to your payment method (i.e. card)* since changing the eater compensation this article wasn’t changed which will cause some mislead with the T&C 5.2.


*Failed Orders*

Also, in Portugal, we have a compensation procedure for failed orders which is not in the KB. Can this be added as we have at least 35% failed orders weekly. 

They follow the below procedure 



* If orders were active for >30m before being failed, agents should call the eater and explain what happened, apologize and inform them we will be adding compensation to their balance for the poor service
* The compensation baseline should be a small comp value (3€), but for extreme cases and on a case-by-case basis could be higher
* This compensation should be added to a previous order, and a note should be made on the eater’s profile:
* _Failed order >30m (OID XXXXX) - compensated X€ on OID XXXXX_
* If the user has no orders yet, we can inform them that *after* making their first order, they can contact us to receive the aforementioned compensation. In these cases agents must leave a note on the profile both times:
* Reporting the user will contact us again: _Failed order >30m (OID XXXXX) - eater’s first order, will contact again for compensation_
Confirmation after the credit is made: _Compensation for failed order on 1.03.2022 issued on OID XXXXX_

3.1.          Authorization of the vehicles supplying the Store

If Bolt Services Ro will use its own fleet for supplying the Store, each vehicle will need to be authorized by the DSVSA for the supply of food products. If the transport of products of animal or non-animal origin will be carried out through the logistical services of a contractual partner, the authorization obligation falls on the latter.

In this sense Order no. 57/2010, provides in Annex 1, Chap. II, point 4, the fact that the means of transport of food of animal origin (including all the vehicles) must be properly equipped so that the products of animal origin do not change their characteristics during transport. The same requirement is established for the transport of food of non-animal origin, according to Annex no. 9, Chapter VI, point 7 of Order no. 111/2008. This means that the vehicle used for the supply of the Store must be able to maintain the temperature of the products, according to the manufacturer's specifications (from the packaging) throughout transportation. This aspect is also stressed by the provisions of Order no. 976/1998 which provide that easily alterable foods (dairy products, eggs, etc.) will be transported with refrigerated means of transport, provided and equipped with means of ventilation and refrigeration, including equipment for temperature control and recording. This authorization will need to be obtained by the Store in the case of supply of own means of transport.

For the means of transport which transport products of animal origin and that meet the sanitary-veterinary conditions, DSVSA issues the sanitary veterinary and for food safety authorization (to be obtained for each vehicle used for transport).

The following documents will need to be submitted in order to obtain the sanitary veterinary and food safety authorization for the means of transport.

(a)            the application for authorization, specifying the transport capacity, the thermal regime, the types of products that can be transported and the registration number of the means of transport;

(b)            copy of the registration certificate of the means of transport;

(c)             the document certifying that the authorization fees have been paid, according to the legislation in force.

*For the delivery of food and non-food products within the city limits or on a route which does not exceed 4 hours, there is an exception from the authorization requirements of the vehicles, as according to the provisions of Order no. 976/1998, such delivery may be done with isotherm containers (i.e. the Bolt Food bags) without the need to obtain an authorization for the rider’s vehicle from DSVSA.*

Hey Jimmy,

So it is technically possible but not exactly in the setup you’ve mentioned. First of all, we cannot randomly create an invoice for X amount. Invoices are created by our system based on certain rules depending on the service. However, you might use a concept called “Provider Business”, which technically, in terms of invoicing, brings all providers of a certain vendor under one business. In this model, for all the providers, we generate only 1 aggregated invoice under the name of the main vendor. And this invoice also includes a row for “free delivery” cost. The vendor can simply use this amount to determine how much they would pay, but unfortunately we cannot create an invoice for a designated amount. So, you can switch this vendor to Provider Business for the period and then switch back to separate invoicing afterwards. The other setback for this model is, separate providers will not get any separate invoices whatsoever. There will only be 1 aggregated invoice for all the services under the vendor.

Another option can be [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/3471114383/Cost-sharing+V2+Model|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BF/pages/3471114383/Cost-sharing+V2+Model|smart-link], which honestly I am not quite experienced with but in this model, there will be separate invoices for each provider with a row called “campaign fee”. The setbacks for this model is: 1) there won’t be an aggregated invoice, each provider will get a separate invoice, 2) the row in the invoice is not called “free delivery”.

In my opinion, the second option is a better fit to your request if the vendor doesn’t mind getting separate invoices for each provider instead of 1 aggregated invoice.

Share the following message to local teams:

----

Hey team\! As some of you might know I've been doing a small deep-dive into manual adjustments for some of the largest markets & my goal was to determine how many duplicate rows (/adjustments) we actually upload on a regular basis. From the initial analysis I noticed the global numbers were pretty alarming but after having a chat with some of you how the process goes I was pleasantly surprised that things aren't actually that bad I thought

As the realistic impact is small we've decided we're not going to pull in our developers to build something for duplicate entries but as we know with such manual process mistakes can & will happen (especially for a huge market like the UK) so I'm proposing a small addition to the currently used sheet where we collect our manual adjustments to flag the duplicate rows directly in the Sheets. I added a new column on the copy called Validation & the formula goes something like this

{noformat}=ARRAYFORMULA(IF(ISBLANK(D2:D),, IF(COUNTIFS(D:D, $D2:D,E:E,E2:E, F:F,F2:F, G:G, G2:G, I:I, I2:I)>1, "Duplicate", "Unique"))){noformat}

The logic is pretty simple:

# Checks if the driver ID column is populated (column D) -> if no then do nothing / if yes then does the following:
# Gets the driver id (D) + order id (E) + amount (F) + ticket link (G) + adjustment subtype (I) & counts all of the _unique_ rows
# And if the count is >1 prints out Duplicate
# Otherwise prints Unique

Then I've added conditional formatting to easily detect the duplicate rows in the sheet & some nice graphs as well for duplicate vs unique rows. But this is all optional

So in general we're not going to say that do not upload duplicate adjustments (as it can happen of course) but just throwing this out here to maybe help the agents avoid unnecessary duplicate adjustments. Attaching some of the screenshots & here's the [link|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dkTtaQ-DkRInFA9XE873ITGi_WEnNwmmTMfExmjQFvA/edit#gid=0] to the copy as well if interested. Appreciate any feedback as usual

* I don't think this Route53 IP-based routing option will work for two reasons: 1. It doesn't support Private Hosted Zones and 2. Route 53 Resolver doesn't support edns0 (for passing the private ip of the client to the upstream domain servers). You could of course try to point your Nodes to Google DNS and then try to use the Elastic IPs of your zonal NAT Gateways in Route53 IP-based routing, but not sure how well this would work and to be honest it would be quite hacky?

* Another option would be to create an internal load balancer (ALB/NLB) in each AZ and then point workloads in each AZ to the zone-internal load balancer, that would have the Envoy instances in its Target Group.

* You could also create a virtual IP in the VPC and then use use Route Table in each subnet to point that VIP to a zone-local Envoy instance (although if you have many Envoys in each AZ, then not sure this option would work).

* Since this is EKS, a Kubernetes-native option would be use Topology Aware Hints \[1]. From Kubernetes documentation: "Topology Aware Hints provides a mechanism to help keep traffic within the zone it originated from". This feature should be enabled in the upcoming Kubernetes/EKS version 1.24 that is scheduled to come out end of this year (since EKS typically uses the upstream default for all features). We have some EKS customers who are waiting for this. Would it be possible for you to wait as well? I think this would be the best option\!

Small correction related to edns0:

Route 53 Resolver (the VPC internal DNS server) does support EDNS0 (the generic extension mechanism) but does not support EDNS Client Subnet (the specific extension option) for this purpose.

Yes, sure. In a nutshell the issue is the following: 

Some drivers who operate on our platform have for several years issued invoices to their clients for transportation services without VAT even though they were actually liable for VAT. This mistake happened mainly because Bolt (who issues the invoices on behalf of the drivers) incorrectly marked these drivers in our system as non-VAT liable. 

Despite this technical mishap from Bolt side it still the drivers, who are responsible for the payment of the VAT since they are the ones who issue the invoice to the clients. The VAT liable drivers should have noticed that their invoices are incorrect, issued new correct invoices (or ask for a reissue from Bolt) and forward the VAT to the tax authority. The VAT amount is in the possession of the drivers since the ride fare that they collected is in any case VAT inclusive.

We now want to know if there are any tax related obligations for Bolt because of this incident. We don’t see any possibility that Bolt should be liable for the VAT that the drivers didn’t pay but are there any administrative or other sanctions that Bolt may face due to its role in incorrectly marking the drivers as non-VAT liable?

This question and answer to it is definitely tax related and it can come from our budget.

Another question is a legal one that you may be willing to explore yourselves (with your budget): do the drivers have any civil law claims against us for any damages that they may have due to this mistake?

{noformat}with tz as (select id city_id, name, timezone tz from public.admin_system_city)

, menu_views as (SELECT menu.mp_insert_id,
                 timestamp 'epoch' + menu.time * interval '1 second' as menu_viewed_time,
                  menu.haspromo, menu.cityid as city_id, menu.providerid as provider_id,
                  substring(menu.distinct_id, 10, len(menu.distinct_id) - 10 + 1) as user_id
                FROM ext_mixpanel_bolt_food.menu_viewed menu
                where date(menu_viewed_time) >='2022-06-01')

select
menu_views.city_id                 as city_id
, menu_views.provider_id                  as provider_id
, count (menu_views.user_id)     as menu_viewers

left join tz on tz.city_id = menu_views.city_id
WHERE (( CONVERT_TIMEZONE(tz.tz,oo.created)  ) >= '2022-09-05 00:00:00' AND ( CONVERT_TIMEZONE(tz.tz,oo.created)  ) < '2022-09-12 00:00:00')

AND menu_views.provider_id=2860
group by 1,2

* _driver violates the rule of parking his car in the airport only in connection with Bolt RH services and his parking fee is more than EUR 50 -_ more than 20 eur (with new approach).

* _Driver approaches Bolt to pay his / her parking fee that Bolt has already paid to Unipark -_ yes, driver contacts the CS and expresses the wish to be back in the parking system so he / she could entre the parking for free.
* _driver pays the fee to Bolt -_ we deduct the fee from his balance.
* _we reinstate driver’s discount to park at Unipark parking lot -_ we put driver’s car’s license plate numbers back to the parking system and he can enter it for free.



Transactions:

* _driver reimburses the same parking fee to Bolt -_ in this case, yes, if after the violation he / she wants to get back to the system, he / she pays from the balance to us (because we have already paid for the parking)

	from tunisia_drivers td
	where td.date < date('2022-07-01')
	group by 1, 2, 3, 4

	from tunisia_drivers td
	where td.date >= date('2022-07-01')

	group by 1, 2, 3, 4

	coalesce(fd.company_name, fc."name", fc2."name") as company_name,
	coalesce(fd.company_id, fc.id) as company_id,
	meb.*, 
	cac.positive_balance_after, 
	least(greatest(-meb.month_end_balance, 0), coalesce(cac.positive_balance_after, 0)) as collection_of_meb
	from month_end_balance meb
	left join collection_after_cutoff cac on cac.client_id = meb.client_id and cac.currency = meb.currency

* Identification (ID or passport)
* If the courier is not a Cypriot national, verify whether the courier has a right to reside in Cyprus (e.g. visa) and whether the courier is legally permitted to work under the terms of his right to reside;
* If the courier will be making deliveries using a vehicle (motorbike, car etc.), drivers’ licence and insurance;
* Bank details to facilitate the making of payments;
* It may also be advisable to verify whether the courier is registered for tax and social security, although as noted above, if the courier is considered an independent contractor, it is the courier’s responsibility to account for income tax and social security.

The discrepancy in the "savings" calculations is coming from the fact that the entire sum of compensations was taken into account while applying the VAT to it, where in fact, in most of the markets, we are already netting some part of compensations. Therefore, it should be calculated by the not-netted compensation sum instead. For example;
 _In Nigeria, we already netted 5M€ worth of compensations - but didn't net 250K€ (in 2021)_
_So the calculation should actually be done for 250K€. As this is the amount we will save from by netting compensations._
_Therefore the apprx. saving would be 250k x 7,5% VAT = 18k€ only._


The new calculations are here in this sheet: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1loAtdkHH4AapHZhYcC3Ppxy2W-IaW5d44Z9Noe3nvcw/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1loAtdkHH4AapHZhYcC3Ppxy2W-IaW5d44Z9Noe3nvcw/edit#gid=0|smart-link]

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] thanks so much for those additional details.

According to my research, price is mandatory pre-contractual information to be provided to consumers in the T&Cs. Although unilateral change of price would be considered as unfair practice, *under FR consumer law there’s no specific minimum prior notice to notify changes of price and T&Cs* . 

Only communication service providers shall serve 30-day prior notice in the event of changes to T&Cs.

However, under *P2B* regulation applicable to *business users only*, prior notice must be served in the event of changes to terms and conditions. Prior notice period shall be:

*  at least 15 days from the date on which the provider of online intermediation services notifies the business users concerned about the proposed changes. 
* > 15 days if changes trigger technical or commercial adaptations to be implemented by business users. 

Starting *from 2024 Digital Services Act* will require to notify users of changes to T&Cs. I’m not aware of any mandatory prior notice but I’ve asked Regulatory to provide the final approved text to have a look into details.

Hope this helps and please do let me know if you need further details.

Hi everyone, the document list from our side was created after research and alignment with local employment legislation and meetings with several government departments.
Priority was to make sure we are operating with a model avoiding any risks and penalties for the company and our courier partners.

*(*cases like the one we had prior transition and in which we had to pay a big fine for Couriers stopped by the Police.)*

Explanation on extra document we request:
{color:#ff5630}Picture of driver's license (both sides) - if the vehicle chosen is a car or motorbike;{color}
We verify the courier is legally able to drive the type of vehicle indicated to complete Bolt Food orders. 
Comment based on experience - 
Importance: *Critical - Mandatory*

{color:#ff5630}Vehicle photo that clearly shows the vehicle and its number plates - if the vehicle chosen is a car or motorbike;{color}
Its common for us to receive calls either from civilians or police asking for details of specific couriers with reference their vehicle number plates. Although we are not giving any information to anyone beside police we want to have at least a reference of the vehicle that the couriers use to complete orders. It can be consider as Quality control check as well.
Comment based on experience - Importance: *High*

{color:#ff5630}Marriage Certificate - only for third-country nationals;{color}
Its an official document that confirms partner visa status

Importance: *Critical - Mandatory*

{color:#ff5630}Mobile phone Contract or recent Bill showing full name, address and phone number;{color}
This was added after cases we had when Police had campaigns for checking legal documents of third country nationals. For us to be able to find a specific courier we always use telephone number as a reference and as an extra step of confirmation we ask courier to provide the contract with their supplier indicating the number belongs to them.

Comment based on experience - 
Importance: *Medium*

Best,

Christos
